papers.title: Developing the Longitudinal Study of Aging in Guatemala (ELEGUA): Rationale and pilot protocol
papers.reason: This aging-cohort protocol may support general longitudinal cognitive assessment, but the available title provides no specific connection to executive function or computational modelling.

papers.title: Cognitive assessment in heart failure: clinical value, timing, and practical tools
papers.reason: The paper concerns practical cognitive assessment in a clinical population, but the available information does not identify an executive-function focus or a digital or multimodal biomarker method.

papers.title: An LLM-supported just-in-time adaptive intervention delivered by a socially assistive robot for cognitive training in mild cognitive impairment: study protocol for an assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial
papers.reason: This human MCI trial uses adaptive multidomain cognitive training and exploratory imaging biomarkers, but its primary focus is intervention efficacy rather than executive-function modelling or multimodal classification.

papers.title: Determinants of Cognitive Change Over 1 Year in Older Adults With Type 1 Diabetes
papers.reason: The study identifies clinical predictors of longitudinal MoCA and processing-speed change, but it does not specifically model executive processes or develop a digital biomarker.

papers.title: Chinese medicine interventions for cerebral small vessel disease-related cognitive impairment: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.reason: This meta-analysis evaluates treatment effects on global MoCA and MMSE scores rather than executive-function mechanisms, neuroscience findings, or digital assessment.

papers.title: Cognitively engaging sedentary activities are associated with better cognitive function in middle-aged adults: a cross-sectional study using the 1970 British Cohort Study
papers.reason: The study includes verbal fluency and cancellation measures relevant to executive control and attention, but its central contribution is a cross-sectional lifestyle association with global cognition.

papers.title: Risk factors and development of a predictive model for post-traumatic cognitive impairment in patients with frontal lobe cerebral contusion
papers.reason: The paper predicts post-traumatic cognitive impairment from clinical risk factors in frontal-lobe injury, but it uses global screening outcomes rather than executive-function process measures or digital biomarkers.

papers.title: Exploring the Relationship Between Sleep Disturbances, Gut Microbiota, and Cognition in Patients with Heart Failure: A Cross-Sectional Study
papers.reason: The study relates sleep and microbiota measures to global MoCA performance in heart failure, with no specific analysis of executive function or computational cognitive mechanisms.

papers.title: Age-Group Differences in the Temporal Structure of Speech and Forehead total-Hb Responses During a Phonemic Verbal Fluency Task: A Comparison of Adults in Their 40s and 70s
papers.reason: The study reports age-related differences in verbal-fluency dynamics and concurrent forehead hemodynamic responses, providing behavioural and neural features potentially useful for modelling executive retrieval and aging.

papers.title: Cognitive performance determinants in competitive fencing: a systematic review
papers.reason: This review synthesizes human evidence on visual attention, anticipation, response selection, and inhibition under time pressure, offering findings relevant to models of attention and cognitive control.
